definition: Reuse and preparing-for-reuse profile: requirements for objects re-entering use for the same purpose (waste-hierarchy-preferred routes), per the Waste Framework Directive

manifest.issuing_role: refurbisher / dealer (EN 18239 role set); condition attestations by qualified attestor as lens-scoped stamps

legal_basis.citation: Art. 4 (waste hierarchy — preparing for reuse ranked second only to prevention); Art. 3(13) re-use; Art. 3(16) preparing for re-use

legal_basis.instrument: Directive (EU) 2024/1799 on common rules promoting the repair of goods
EN 18239 (data carriers and access control for DPP)

manifest.notes: Reuse is the loop's cheapest closure and the identity-conserving one: the object keeps its passport (I1); events append (E7 refurbish, E1 custody transfer, E14 condition stamps). Closed installation intervals carry harvested-part provenance, which is the value carrier of the re-use market. Preparing-for-reuse on a subject already in waste status runs through P4's re-qualification machinery where the law requires it; the two profiles compose on the same identity.

triggers.description: refurbish / preparing-for-re-use operation on the subject (E7 event class), or custody transfer to a re-use channel with a condition stamp
